name: What is included in a retail tenant improvement scope?

mainEntity.name: What is usually included in a retail tenant improvement scope for a storefront build-out?
mainEntity.text: What is usually included in a retail tenant improvement scope for a storefront build-out?

acceptedAnswer.text: A retail tenant improvement scope is the construction work needed to make a leased commercial space usable for a specific store concept. Typical scope items include demolition of existing finishes, new partitions, drywall, flooring, ceiling systems, lighting, electrical distribution, HVAC modifications, plumbing for restrooms or sinks, paint, casework, and storefront details. In many projects, the scope also includes accessibility upgrades, fire/life-safety items, and landlord-required improvements. The exact scope depends on the space condition, the lease terms, and the business type. Retail tenants should confirm which items are part of base-building work, which are landlord responsibilities, and which are tenant costs before signing. A clear scope document helps prevent budget overruns and change-order disputes later in the project.
acceptedAnswer.description: A retail tenant improvement scope usually includes demolition, framing, drywall, flooring, ceilings, lighting, electrical, HVAC modifications, restrooms, storefront finishes, paint, fixtures, and code-related upgrades. Depending on the lease and concept, it may also include ADA access improvements, signage preparation, and millwork for display and checkout areas.
